mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate, indicating tighter monetary conditions, leads to a decrease in the S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of cases when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 returns are positive in over 50% of periods following a 0.3pp UNRATE increase, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates reduced demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST below 1600 doesn't correlate with negative returns (p > 0.1), the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production suggests supply issues, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decline doesn't predict negative returns (t-test p > 0.05), hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth indicates strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 growth doesn't correlate with positive returns (Rank IC < 0.03), hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment alongside stable employment suggests labor market stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive in >40% of cases with rising UNRATE and stable PAYEMS, hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Rising FEDFUNDS with high CPIAUCSL indicates inflation concerns, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If hypothesis doesn't hold (p > 0.05), it's rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, rising UNRATE signals slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If returns are positive in >50% of triggered cases, hypothesis fails.
